findings.text: the figcaptions (183, 188, 193, 198) and the panel legend at scripts/prototypes/diiid_stopping_rule/render_terminal_panels.py:327 name the EFIT contour's lowest vertex an "EFIT X-point", while the record's own body at :130 correctly calls it "the low point of its EFIT contour"; on 179 limited the marked point is R 1.53 m, Z -0.95 m, 0.25 m from the reference X-point near (1.3, -1.1) m the root-cause record gives, so the caption names a null the mark is not.

"the two coincide to the millimetre -- R 1.382 m, Z -1.061 m for both -- ... which is itself the reading" reads exact equality of two float32-rounded coordinates as independent agreement; identity to eight significant figures is what one shared datum produces rather than two measurements agreeing, and the lattice under those numbers is 5.3 cm in R and 10 cm in Z (geometry-limiter-137-diverted.npz grid_r/grid_z), so a millimetre claim is an order of magnitude finer than the grid.

_check_layout tests only whether a text artist lies inside the axes box and whether two text artists overlap, while the repository figure rule also requires refusing a text artist whose bounding box extends beyond the canvas; a label clipped off the edge passes this check silently, and no test or committed log records the check firing other than the conservative-smoke refusal quoted from resume-8.jsonl.

_efit_axis re-implements the capability nova/equilibrium/stencil_nulls.py:1891 magnetic_axis_subgrid owns -- "return the resolved magnetic axis on a rectangular grid" -- taking the same (field, rg, zg, inside) operands it takes, and neither extends nor wraps the owner; the recorder's docstring claims centimetre reporting over a lattice whose spacing is 5.3 cm in R and 10 cm in Z, so the duplicate is also the coarser of the two.
